title: Fit a wheel cover onto a car's steel wheel with its valve notch over the valve stem and every retaining clip snapped in
instruction: Put the wheel cover on the wheel.
context: Plastic wheel covers on steel wheels come off for every tyre change, rotation and puncture repair and go back on by hand, on the driveway or in the tyre shop, with the wheel on the car. The cover has one notch for the valve stem and must be turned until that notch is over the stem before it is pushed on: pushed on anywhere else it lands on the stem, will not clip down on that side and can crush or tear the stem. A cover left loose falls off on the road.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of their midpoint) in cm; heights are above the ground the arms stand on, which is the car's ground. Wheel (on the car, held still): black-painted 13 x 4.5J pressed-steel wheel (3 mm steel, 36.5 cm across the flanges, 33.0 cm bead seat, 4 x 100 mm studs with four zinc wheel nuts, on a brake drum 21 cm across) with a black 155/80 R13 tyre (57.8 cm across, 15.5 cm wide), upright, its axle along x at y 0 and 27.2 cm up (the tyre's loaded radius; its footprint flat on the ground), its outboard face towards the robot with the outboard flange's face at x 42.0. Valve stem: black rubber snap-in stem (TR414 class) with a black cap, 1.1 cm across, at the top of the rim, 14.2 cm above the axle, its cap 1.2 cm out from the flange's face. Car body round the wheel arch: a flat, vertical, blue-painted steel body side with its outer face at x 43.0 (2.5 cm inboard of the tyre's sidewall), from y -60 to 60 and from 17 cm (its lower edge) to 72 cm up, with an arch opening 34.5 cm in radius about the axle, open below the axle down to the lower edge, a rolled lip round the opening, a black plastic arch liner 22 cm deep over the tyre and black sills 6 cm deep along the lower edge. Wheel cover: 13-inch silver ABS hubcap, 36.0 cm across, 4.2 cm deep, 0.45 kg, with a dark 6.4 cm centre cap, one valve notch 3.35 cm wide cut in from its edge to 12.5 cm from its centre, eight through slots (4 cm radially, about 4.8 cm wide) between eight 2.4 cm spokes, and eight black retaining clips on a sprung steel ring under its rim, reaching 3.7 cm behind its lip. It lies face up on the ground, resting on its clips, centred at (20, 0), with its notch pointing 67.5 degrees to the right of straight ahead. Distractors (NVIDIA SimReady, loose on the ground, not scored): an orange microfibre cleaning cloth (cleaning_cloth_a01, 26 x 23 x 2 cm, 50 g) at (33, 34) turned 15 degrees; a pair of blue light-duty nitrile gloves (ppe_gloves_lightDuty_a01, 25 x 23 cm, 60 g) at (35, -35) turned -20 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Each step, in the wheel's frame: a clip is seated when its catching face is hooked behind the bead seat's lip (at least 1.0 mm out past the lip's inner face and behind its back edge, within 0.5 mm) and the cover's lip beside it is within 1.0 mm of the flange. The stem is through the notch when its cap is within 1.1 cm of the notch's centre line, between 12.5 and 18.0 cm from the cover's centre and inside the cover's depth (3.0 cm behind to 2.0 cm in front of its lip). 1.0: the stem through the notch, all eight clips seated and every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) at least 3 cm from the cover, all held 2 s; the trial ends there. Otherwise, at the end: the stem through the notch scores 0.2 plus 0.075 per seated clip (0.2 to 0.8); the stem not through the notch scores 0. A stem ever bent more than 15 degrees from its rest scores 0 for the whole trial.
reset_notes: Pull the cover off (fingers behind its rim beside a clip), check the stem stands straight and undamaged (replace it if bent or torn) and lay the cover face up on the ground at (20, 0), notch 67.5 degrees right of straight ahead, centred within 5 mm. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies. No SimReady wheel, tyre, car body or hubcap exists, so all are custom meshes; the wheel is held still, as on a parked car, and the body is only the side round the arch. The ABS cover is rigid (a real one flexes). Its steel ring is eight sprung clips, 1,500 N/m each; pushing it on took about 110 N at peak from both arms. A real cover's push-on force is unmeasured (README). The stem is a sprung hinge. Uniform friction, no click, no force sensing.
